entities.name: PMID:27493455
observations: Alnouti et al. studied dexamethasone in primary human hepatocytes cultured on collagen or Matrigel, with RU486 used to assess glucocorticoid-receptor involvement.
Dexamethasone increased CYP8B1 mRNA and increased cholic-acid formation while decreasing chenodeoxycholic-acid formation.
The abstract did not report CYP8B1 protein, enzyme activity, flux, or numerical effect sizes.

entities.name: Dexamethasone
observations: In primary human hepatocyte cultures, dexamethasone increased CYP8B1 mRNA and shifted bile-acid formation toward more cholic acid and less chenodeoxycholic acid.

entities.name: CYP8B1
observations: Dexamethasone directly increased CYP8B1 transcript abundance in primary human hepatocytes; direct protein or enzyme-activity induction was not reported in the accessible abstract.

entities.name: Cholic acid
observations: Cholic-acid formation increased after dexamethasone exposure in primary human hepatocyte cultures.

entities.name: Chenodeoxycholic acid
observations: Chenodeoxycholic-acid formation decreased after dexamethasone exposure in primary human hepatocyte cultures.

entities.name: Mifepristone
observations: RU486/mifepristone experiments were used to evaluate glucocorticoid-receptor involvement; the authors interpreted CYP8B1 induction as largely glucocorticoid-receptor independent.
